messages.subject: Meet and Analyze Data, Wed June 6th
messages.subject_clean: Meet and Analyze Data, Wed June 6th
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

we will be having a Meet and Analyze Data session from 3:00pm-5:00pm
today (06/06), in the Bennett conference room of the Center for
Companion Animal Health
(http://www.vetmed.ucdavis.edu/ccah/ccah-secure/bennett-conf-room.cfm).
Hope to see you there!

--

If you think you are going to join us, please let us know --

https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeUW5QS55uDwDpusGYerY542D_tQubkmPMtUKlGdbmoSWfSSQ/viewform

--

Meet and Analyze Data (MAD) is a forum to bring your biological big
data and discuss high level concept problems (what is metagenome
assembly?) and low level coding problems (what does this error message
even mean?!) and everything in between. There is no scheduled or
specific activity: people show up with questions about how to analyze
their data, or maybe they are willing to help others. We typically get
questions about experimental design for
transcriptomic/metagenomic/genomic projects, or how to install
software, or how to run their analysis on clusters or the cloud.

Cheers,
Luiz Irber

messages.body_plain:
Hi R-users,

The Data Management Program at the UC Davis library is looking to hire a student assistant with R and data management skills for our pilot STRIDE (Successful Transformation of a Research Idea into Data Engagement) incubator this summer. The posting is on Aggie Job Link https://ucdavis-csm.symplicity.com/students/index.php?s=jobs&ss=jobs&mode=form&id=5f5681ca66912d0dc5f091e676fee234 or you can search by job id 839980.
Let me know if you have any questions (or have trouble accessing the post).

Vessela Ensberg

Associate Director, Data Management Program

Data and Digital Scholarship Department

UC Davis Library

messages.subject: raster::predict() returning NAs
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am using the raster package in R to predict the result of a classification model I fitted using SVM (caret package). I've done this before with the same study area and it worked just fine. Google does not have good answers for this problem, so I was wondering if anyone in this listserve knows how to fix this.

Because my study area is non-rectangle, my raster has rows with 0 and NA values.

> test_pred_all <- raster::predict(svm_05082018_Radial_Landsatlike, newdata = all)

This is the warning message,
kernlab class probability calculations failed; returning NAs
 So basically, all of my 26 classes are returning NA values:

> summary(test_pred_all)
       1        2        3        4        5        6        7        8
       0        0        0        0        0        0        0        0
       9       10       11       12       13       14       15       16
       0        0        0        0        0        0        0        0
      17       18       19       20       21       23       24       25
       0        0        0        0        0        0        0        0
      28     NA's
       0 24490842

This is how I trained my model using SVM from the caret package

> svm_05082018_Radial_Landsatlike <- train(Class ~ Band1_0624+Band2_0624+Band3_0624+Band4_0624+Band8_0624+Band9_0624+Band11_0624+Band12_0624+NDVI_0624+NDWI_0624+Band1_1201+Band2_1201+Band3_1201+Band4_1201+Band8_1201+Band9_1201+Band11_1201+Band12_1201+NDVI_1201+NDWI_1201+dNDVI+dNDWI, data = training_20160624_20161201_def, method = "svmRadial",
                                         trControl=trctrl,
                                         preProcess = c("center", "scale"),
                                         tuneLength = 10)

This is my data frame structure (values from bands are 0 since I applied a mask, and vegetation indices are NAs):

> head(all)

messages.body_plain:
Hi Ana,
I've been dealing with similar issues lately working with gbm models. Do the zero values in your dataset represent missing data? If so, probably want to convert those to NA. Same question and recommendation for the NaN values. Does SVM work with missing data? Have you tried using na.action = na.pass in the train function?
Thanks,
Katie

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: RStudio Server
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Kenji.  It doesn't appear that anyone  has responded to your
query.  If you still need help, let me suggest that you might want to
elaborate on your requirements.  If this is (mostly) for your personal
use, you can:

(1) always run a shiny app on your own machine:

    https://www.rstudio.com/products/shiny/download-server/

(2) download the open-source edition of Rstudio server:

    https://www.rstudio.com/products/rstudio/download-server/

I don't know what campus-wide (or department-wide) resources might be
available to you.

-- Mike
